claims.text: P15 (invariants tier): changed, removed, reordered and inserted entries before the head are detected and the first bad entry is named. A chain rebuilt after a change, removal or reorder, with every hash recomputed, is detected against the head file. Removing the head entry, an entry added after the recorded head, and a missing or unreadable head file are all detected.

Torn last entry: a line cut at any point, and a complete line the head file does not yet record, are both reported as torn and named as entry n+1. Appends are refused until drop_torn_entry is confirmed, and the drop is itself logged. A crash during the drop leaves the torn log unchanged.
Failure modes / external calls: not applicable. case.py makes no network or other external calls. It does only local file I/O, using os.open, os.write, fsync, os.replace and flock.

Failure modes / idempotency: each append is guarded by the expected log position, which acts as its idempotency key. Retrying an append that already succeeded raises LogConflict and changes neither the log nor the head file. A stale position likewise writes nothing.
claims.proof_output: 1 passed, 102 deselected in 0.10s (test_retrying_an_append_that_already_succeeded_writes_nothing_twice); test_stale_expected_position_is_a_conflict_and_writes_nothing passes in the full suite

claims.text: Failure modes / retries and dead-letter path: not applicable. There is no queue or consumer, and a locked case fails fast with CaseLocked rather than retrying. The only retry is a bounded re-read (READ_RETRIES=5, 20 ms pause) so that a reader does not report a writer caught between its two writes as a torn entry.
claims.proof_cmd: python -m pytest -q tests/test_case_log.py -k 'reader_during_an_append or second_writer or another_process'
claims.proof_output: passes within the 103 passed in tests/test_case_log.py

claims.text: Failure modes / partial failure is repairable: if power is lost mid-line, after the line but before the head file, or during a drop, the log is left either torn (repaired with drop_torn_entry, which is recorded) or intact. Both the head file and the dropped log are written to a temporary file, fsynced and renamed.

Data / additive and reversible: the change only adds files (src/cma/case.py, tests/test_case_log.py). It changes no existing module, schema or fixture, so there is nothing to backfill, and rolling back means not calling it or reverting the commit. The full suite and the offline evals are unchanged.

claims.proof_output: (no other files changed); 373 passed in 10.61s; 9/9 memos fully grounded; model = fake

claims.text: Data / PII: entry data can hold case details. The log, lock and head files are created mode 0600. Error messages name entries by number only and never quote their content.
claims.proof_output: passes within the 103 passed (test_new_log_and_lock_files_are_private_to_their_owner now also asserts the head file's mode)

claims.text: Security / input validated at the boundary: event must be a non-empty string. data must be plain JSON that reads back unchanged, so NaN, Infinity, tuples, non-string keys and text that cannot be encoded as UTF-8 (lone surrogates) are refused. Lines on disk are decoded strictly: no duplicate members, no non-finite numbers, canonical bytes only, and deep nesting is named rather than raised.

notes: GAPS FOR THE OWNER. (1) No production caller: nothing in src/ calls CaseLog yet (grep finds no caller), so by the project gotcha R42/R43 are not done until T27 (sign-off) and the import, override and preview commands record into it and call require_intact before signing. Wiring callers belongs to those tasks, not T12. (2) Observability: there is no structured log line or alert yet. The design's event lines (event=..., case id, counts) and the red-banner refusal on CaseLogBroken belong to the callers (C3 commands, C5, C6). Dashboards are not applicable: by design nothing leaves the machine. (3) Operability: the module needs no feature flag because it is opt-in by calling it, and rollback is not calling it or reverting the commit; that rollback was not tried in any non-production environment. There is no runbook entry for a torn or broken log; the user-facing steps (confirm drop_torn_entry, and what to do when the chain is broken) belong with the command that exposes them. There are no config or secret changes to deploy. (4) Performance: not a configured tier, so not claimed. A local scratch measurement showed append is O(n) because every append re-verifies the whole chain: about 19 ms at 500 entries and 76 ms at 2,000 entries (660 KB). That is fine for event logs of hundreds of entries, but nothing bounds the size of one entry's data or the number of entries; whether to cap either is a design decision. There are no queries or list endpoints. (5) Docs: no API doc, ADR or changelog line was added; the module docstring documents the format and the head-file contract. A release note in user terms should land with the first command that writes a case log. (6) Known limit, recorded in the docstring: rewriting the log and the head file together is not detectable from these files alone; the sign-off or pack must pin the head it saw (T27). (7) The case directory's own permissions (mkdir uses the default umask) are R31/C3 case-root work, not T12.
